stories.title: Secret Claude tracker shocks users after Anthropic’s anti-surveillance stance
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Anthropic, developer of Claude, is accused of secretly tracking its users.
The controversy directly contradicts Anthropic's stated commitment to anti-surveillance practices.
An internal engineer has reportedly confirmed the tracking was a temporary 'experiment' that has been discontinued.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.

bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The speedup is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster specifically when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released as an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware for optimized execution.
The feature is currently available in a preview state.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local, on-device operation.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI agents privately on the user's own hardware.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command to streamline the setup and execution of coding tools.
It enables running advanced coding models (e.g., Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex) locally or in the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: Microsoft is selling off four Xbox studios as part of significant gaming cuts
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is implementing significant layoffs, impacting nearly 4,800 employees, with a large portion concentrated in the Xbox division.
As part of the restructuring, four Xbox game studios are being spun off to operate independently from Microsoft.
The move signals a major strategic shift and consolidation within Microsoft's gaming portfolio.

stories.title: UK regulator warns of "arms race" to keep up with AI use in financial services
stories.author: Martin Arnold
bullet_points: UK regulator (FCA) is concerned about an 'arms race' developing around AI adoption in financial services.
The warning highlights the increasing reliance of millions on AI-driven technology for personal finance decisions.
The regulator is advocating for expanded powers for the watchdog to effectively oversee AI usage in the sector.

stories.title: From Fixed to Free Cameras: Calibration-Free View-Robust Vision-Language-Action Model
stories.author: Ran Xu
bullet_points: Addresses a critical real-world limitation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: fragility when camera setups change.
Proposes a novel approach where the VLA policy self-determines camera pose rather than relying on explicit extrinsic parameters.
Enhances the practical deployability and robustness of robotic systems in dynamic, uncontrolled environments.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
stories.author: Azalia Mirhoseini
bullet_points: Introduces 'verification' as a new, critical scaling axis for Large Language Models (LLMs), moving beyond just compute scaling.
Presents 'LLM-as-a-Verifier,' a novel, general-purpose framework for determining solution correctness in agentic tasks.
The framework provides fine-grained feedback without necessitating additional model training, offering a practical advancement for LLM reliability.

stories.title: Search Beyond What Can Be Taught: Evolving the Knowledge Boundary in Agentic Visual Generation
stories.author: Cong Wei
bullet_points: Addresses the 'world-knowledge bottleneck' in visual generation models, where generators fabricate information outside their training data.
Introduces SearchGen-20K and SearchGen-Bench, new datasets designed to test model performance across diverse, long-tailed, and evolving user requests.
Focuses on pushing the boundaries of agentic visual generation by enabling models to search beyond their fixed training corpora.

stories.title: From Fixed to Free Cameras: Calibration-Free View-Robust Vision-Language-Action Model
stories.author: Ran Xu
bullet_points: Addresses a critical real-world limitation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: fragility when camera setups change.
Proposes a novel approach where the VLA policy learns to be 'calibration-free,' eliminating the need for explicit camera extrinsic information.
Enhances the practical deployability and robustness of robotic systems in dynamic, real-world environments.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
stories.author: Azalia Mirhoseini
bullet_points: Introduces 'verification' as a new scaling axis for improving Large Language Models (LLMs), moving beyond just pre-training and compute.
Presents 'LLM-as-a-Verifier,' a general-purpose framework designed to check the correctness of solutions in agentic tasks.
The framework offers fine-grained feedback for agents without necessitating additional model training.

stories.title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Yuxiao Dong
bullet_points: Addresses the critical limitation of finite context windows in long-horizon agentic LLMs.
Proposes CompactionRL, a novel reinforcement learning strategy to handle extended interaction trajectories.
Utilizes context compaction to summarize past states, allowing agents to operate within constrained context lengths.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
stories.author: Azalia Mirhoseini
bullet_points: Introduces 'verification' as a new, critical scaling axis for Large Language Models (LLMs), alongside compute scaling.
Presents 'LLM-as-a-Verifier,' a novel, general-purpose framework for determining solution correctness.
The framework offers fine-grained feedback for agentic tasks without necessitating additional model training.

stories.title: Ternlight – 7 MB embedding model that runs in browser (WASM)
stories.author: soycaporal
bullet_points: Introduction of Ternlight, a compact 7MB embedding model.
Key feature is its ability to run entirely within the web browser using WebAssembly (WASM).
Represents a significant step towards on-device, low-resource AI inference.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This suggests an advancement in autonomous agent capabilities for coding tasks.

stories.title: Former Xbox studios Double Fine and Compulsion will keep games after going indie
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Microsoft is spinning off four Xbox studios, including Compulsion Games, Double Fine Productions, Ninja Theory, and Undead Labs.
Double Fine and Compulsion will transition to independent operations.
The two independent studios are guaranteed to retain their existing game franchises and catalogs.

stories.title: Nintendo will stop selling the original Switch in Europe next year
stories.author: Andrew Webster
bullet_points: Nintendo is discontinuing the sale of the original Switch in Europe next year.
The successor, Switch 2, will feature a new design element, including a replaceable battery in Europe.
The announcement comes via an updated FAQ detailing hardware revisions for the European market.

stories.title: Kremlin suspected of flying drones over Europe using Russian shadow fleet
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Kremlin is suspected of using drones over Europe.
The drones may have been launched from Russian shadow fleet vessels.
The incident highlights perceived vulnerabilities in European defense readiness.

stories.title: The incredible shrinking Xbox: Five studios, 3,200 employees let go
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Microsoft is undergoing significant workforce reductions within its gaming division.
The layoffs affect approximately 20% of the gaming division's staff, including 3,200 employees across five studios.
The strategic shift involves refocusing development efforts on the company's most established and major franchises.

stories.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Hao Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) when training large language models.
Proposes a 'weak-to-strong' distillation method: training RL on a smaller, cheaper model first.
The learned knowledge from the smaller model is then reused to improve a larger, stronger target model.

stories.title: Interpretable Human-Label-Free Deep Learning for Real-Bogus Classification with Uncertainty Quantification
stories.author: Vincenzo Piuri
bullet_points: Proposes a deep learning framework for Real-Bogus classification in transient surveys without requiring human-labeled data.
Addresses the challenge of noisy or unavailable labels by training on injected transients and bogus-dominated data.
Focuses on robustness against class contamination and provides calibrated uncertainty quantification for reliable classification.

stories.title: What Does a Discrete Diffusion Model Learn?
stories.author: Aran Raoufi
bullet_points: The paper investigates the fundamental learning mechanisms of discrete diffusion models.
It rigorously derives the Continuous-Time Markov Chain (CTMC) Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) for any noising process.
The core contribution is the 'Oracle Distance' theorem, which equates the negative ELBO to a specific metric.

stories.title: Cortex: A Bidirectionally Aligned Embodied Agent Framework for Long-horizon Manipulation
stories.author: Tai Wang
bullet_points: Cortex is a new framework designed to improve embodied AI agents for long-horizon manipulation tasks.
It addresses the limitations of current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, which struggle due to their Markovian nature.
The framework features a bidirectionally aligned system and a customized planning interface to bridge high-level planning and low-level execution.

stories.title: SPEARBench: A Benchmark for Naturalness Evaluation in Streaming Speech-to-Speech Language Models
stories.author: Laureano Moro-Velazquez
bullet_points: SPEARBench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate the naturalness of streaming speech-to-speech language models.
It addresses the limitation of existing benchmarks by focusing on conversational aspects like timing, prosody, and turn-taking.
The benchmark assesses complex qualities such as interpersonal stance and relationship-aware appropriateness in direct speech responses.

stories.title: REDDIT: Correcting Model-Generated Timestamp Drift in ASR without Forgetting via Replay-Based Distribution Editing
stories.author: Hung-yi Lee
bullet_points: Addresses a novel issue in modern ASR: timestamp drift occurring during long non-speech spans.
Proposes a solution using 'Replay-Based Distribution Editing' to correct timestamp inaccuracies without degrading transcription quality.
Evaluates the method across 15 different timestamp-producing ASR systems using custom gap and long-gap benchmarks.

stories.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Hao Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) when training large language models.
Proposes a 'weak-to-strong' distillation method: train RL on a smaller, cheaper model first.
The learned knowledge from the smaller model is then reused to improve a larger, stronger target model.

stories.title: Interpretable Human-Label-Free Deep Learning for Real-Bogus Classification with Uncertainty Quantification
stories.author: Vincenzo Piuri
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of Real-Bogus classification in automated astronomical discovery pipelines.
Proposes a novel deep learning framework capable of training without relying on expensive human-labeled data.
Focuses on robustness against class contamination and provides calibrated uncertainty quantification for reliable results.

stories.title: TabPack: Efficient Hyperparameter Ensembles for Tabular Deep Learning
stories.author: Artem Babenko
bullet_points: Introduces TabPack, a new efficient ensemble method for deep learning on tabular data.
Addresses the limitation of existing ensembles which use uniform hyperparameters, requiring extensive tuning.
TabPack aims for strong out-of-the-box performance while reducing the need for traditional hyperparameter tuning.

stories.title: Fitted Occupancy-Ratio Evaluation without Bellman Completeness
stories.author: Nathan Kallus
bullet_points: Introduces Fitted Occupancy-Ratio Evaluation (FORE) as a new method for off-policy evaluation in reinforcement learning.
FORE bypasses the need for Bellman completeness, addressing limitations in existing primal-dual and minimax estimation methods.
The method characterizes the discounted occupancy ratio using an adjoint Bellman recursion solved via a single-level density-ratio objective.

stories.title: Faithfulness to Refusal: A Causal Audit of Neuron Selectors
stories.author: Vinay Kumar Sankarapu
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap between attribution scores identifying important neurons and proving their causal importance in language models.
The study uses paired audits based on one-shot neuron-row zeroing to test causal faithfulness of neuron selectors.
Attribution methods were shown to significantly outperform baseline methods in identifying dispensable neuron rows at the language-modeling level.

stories.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Hao Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) when training large language models.
Proposes a 'weak-to-strong' distillation method to improve larger target models using knowledge learned from training a smaller, cheaper model.
Focuses on making post-training refinement processes more scalable as language models continue to grow in size.

stories.title: SPEARBench: A Benchmark for Naturalness Evaluation in Streaming Speech-to-Speech Language Models
stories.author: Laureano Moro-Velazquez
bullet_points: Introduces SPEARBench, a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating the naturalness of streaming speech-to-speech language models.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks by focusing on conversational quality factors like timing, prosody, and turn-taking, rather than just standard accuracy.
Targets the growing field of direct spoken query answering systems, highlighting the need for nuanced evaluation beyond simple text/speech metrics.

stories.title: REDDIT: Correcting Model-Generated Timestamp Drift in ASR without Forgetting via Replay-Based Distribution Editing
stories.author: Hung-yi Lee
bullet_points: Addresses a technical flaw in modern autoregressive Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems: timestamp drift during long non-speech spans.
Proposes a novel solution using 'Replay-Based Distribution Editing' to correct timestamp drift without degrading overall model performance.
The research introduces new benchmarks to specifically test and evaluate timestamp generation accuracy in ASR systems.

stories.title: Faithfulness to Refusal: A Causal Audit of Neuron Selectors
stories.author: Vinay Kumar Sankarapu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap between attribution scores (which identify important neurons) and true causal importance in language models.
It introduces two paired audits using one-shot neuron-row zeroing to test the causal significance of identified neuron rows.
The findings suggest that attribution methods are substantially better than simpler activation/magnitude baselines for identifying dispensable rows in language models.

stories.title: Selective Disclosure Watermarking for Large Language Models
stories.author: Qi Long
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in current LLM watermarking: the lack of selective disclosure.
Existing multi-bit watermarking requires revealing the entire embedded message to verify any part of it.
The proposed work aims to enable verifiable, selective disclosure of watermarks within LLM-generated text.

stories.title: How Much is Left? LLMs Linearly Encode Their Remaining Output Length
stories.author: Adam Oberman
bullet_points: The research investigates whether LLMs maintain an internal estimate of their remaining output length.
The study uses linear probes on frozen hidden states of 7-8B open-weight models across various datasets.
Findings suggest predictable token count structures in LLM outputs, such as in step-by-step solutions or retrievals.

stories.title: Observability Design for the AI Era — Application / Infrastructure / CI / LLM, Each in Its Own Shape (Part 1)
stories.author: ryantsuji
bullet_points: The article discusses the necessity of reshaping observability practices to accommodate the demands of the AI era.
It analyzes four distinct axes—Application, Infrastructure, CI, and LLM—each requiring a unique observability design.
Key design decisions highlighted include client-side Gemini cost computation and direct OTel logging to BigQuery.

stories.title: Where Do Your LLM API Keys Actually Live?
stories.author: hadil
bullet_points: Addresses the critical security vulnerability of LLM API key management.
Highlights the risk of dependency compromise leading to credential theft.
Focuses on practical security concerns within LLM application development.

stories.title: I Built a Self-Referential AI System. Then Anthropic Discovered the Same Architecture in Claude.
stories.author: yuhaolin2005
bullet_points: The article discusses the inherent limitations of LLMs, such as concept drift and inability to self-verify.
The author claims to have developed a self-referential AI system to address these limitations.
The core hook is the alleged discovery of a similar architecture by Anthropic in their Claude model.
